newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BEBETO GIVES FLAMENGO DRAW IN VIOLENT MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BEBETO GIVES FLAMENGO DRAW IN VIOLENT MATCH.

text.p: Striker Bebeto scored to earn Flamengo a draw at home against Corinthians at the weekend in a match overshadowed by violence on the field.
The game was marred by a seemingly interminable sequence of crunching tackles, most of which went unpunished by referee Antonio Pereira da Silva.

Flamengo were livid when Corinthians defender Alexandre Lopes was got away with a yellow card for a horrendous challenge from behind on lightweight striker Savio, already suffering from an ankle injury before the game.
They also claimed that Lopes's colleague Gino should have been sent off for bringing down Bebeto, when he had a clear run on goal.
Flamengo were no angels, however, and Corinthians playmaker Souza was carried off after being flattened by Argentine midfielder Alejandro Mancuso.
Former Brazil international Gerson said: "The violence in Brazilian football today is a disgrace. The referees just overlook everything."
Television viewers were able to hear Flamengo coach Joel Santana swearing at match officials during the game, thanks to a microphone near the Flamengo bench.
Marcelinho Carioca put Corinthians in front with a first half penalty but Bebeto, who scored for the second game running, headed in the equaliser in the second half.
There was more brutality elsewhere with match statistics showing 70 fouls during Atletico Paranaense's 2-1 win at home to Vasco da Gama in another game.

Palmeiras lead the first stage of the championship, from which the top eight qualify for the quarter-finals, by four points after beating Santos 2-1 with goals by Colombian international Freddy Rincon and substitute Fernando Dinis.
Former national team goalkeeper Taffarel had a miserable afternoon as his Atletico Mineiro team were on the wrong end of a 5-0 defeat by Gremio.
